items.title: Why Berners-Lee built the web
items.claim: Tim Berners-Lee proposed the World Wide Web at CERN in 1989. What was the immediate motivation?
items.reveal:
Berners-Lee's March 1989 proposal 'Information Management: A Proposal' addressed the problem of staff turnover and lost documentation in a large physics organisation.

CERN released the underlying code into the public domain in 1993.
items.why: Releasing the protocol openly was a choice that shaped the web's evolution.

items.title: Recursion uses stack space
items.claim: A naive recursive Fibonacci function fib(n) = fib(n-1) + fib(n-2) for n=50 will:

options.text: Take roughly 2^50 (~10^15) function calls and either run for hours or exhaust the stack/timeout — naive recursion has exponential complexity even though the iteration is linear
Always crash with a syntax error

items.reveal:
Naive recursive Fibonacci recomputes the same values exponentially many times. Memoisation (caching computed values) or dynamic programming reduces it to O(n) time and O(n) or O(1) space.

Tail-call optimisation (TCO) is a compiler technique to reuse stack frames for tail-recursive calls; Scheme requires it, OCaml supports it, Python doesn't. Functional languages often rely on TCO to make recursion as cheap as iteration.
items.why: Recursion is elegant but not free. Stack depth and redundant work are common pitfalls that can be fixed without abandoning the technique.

items.title: BGP runs the internet on trust
items.claim: BGP (Border Gateway Protocol) is how internet networks decide routes between each other. What is its main security weakness?

options.text: BGP is fully secured by default
Historically, BGP accepted any 'route announcement' from connected networks without cryptographic verification; misconfiguration or malice can hijack traffic globally within minutes
BGP only works inside data centres

items.reveal:
BGP was standardised in 1989 (RFC 1105). It assumes participating networks announce only routes they actually serve. Famous incidents: Pakistan Telecom's 2008 attempt to block YouTube nationally inadvertently routed YouTube traffic globally into a black hole for 2 hours; the 2021 Facebook outage was triggered by a BGP misconfiguration that withdrew Facebook's routes worldwide.

RPKI (Resource Public Key Infrastructure) is being rolled out to cryptographically authenticate route origins, but adoption is partial.
items.why: The internet's most foundational routing protocol assumes goodwill among operators. The system works astonishingly well most of the time and fails spectacularly when it doesn't.
